Regression phase executed against the packet's own subject: do the tests covering this fix bind their claims? ONE mutation check on the guard that closes the named root cause (compiler-disabled test config). Baseline at clean HEAD: focused unit selector on TestIntentCompilerRequiredWhenAssistantHTTPEnabled exited 0 in 96s wall with internal/config reporting 0.091s (executed, not 'no tests to run'). Mutation: the F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED coherence check in internal/config/assistant.go was disabled by short-circuiting its condition. Mutated run FAILED exactly as required — '--- FAIL: TestIntentCompilerRequiredWhenAssistantHTTPEnabled' with 'enabled transport with compiler disabled error = <nil>, want F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED'. Restored with an explicit git checkout as its own step; porcelain verified empty and the guard condition verified present at line 556. Post-restore run exited 0 in 64s. The test therefore binds its claim: removing the fix kills it. Direct grep across all five manifest-required assistant test files found zero t.Skip/t.Skipf/t.SkipNow, and the two bare returns present sit in non-required negative-invariant tests exiting on a false antecedent, not on a failure condition. Adversarial probe recorded a real limitation: regression-quality-guard.sh reports 0 violations on a throwaway file containing nothing but t.Skip and t.Skipf, and its source contains zero skip-family tokens, so its clean result on the five required files is a blind pass rather than skip-freeness evidence. tests/e2e/agent/no_skip_guard_test.go enforces no-skip but scans only its own directory without recursing, so it does not cover tests/e2e/assistant. Skip-freeness is therefore true by content today and mechanically unguarded, which reinforces the already-open TR-BUG-069-005-FRAMEWORK-001 rather than opening a new route. No source file was modified on exit; no DoD item was checked; no certification field was written.
